Yes, when you are in a thread with another user of a differing opinion, who is taking the time to respond, is showing a decent level of critical thinking to both you, and themselves, that requires minimal reading comprehension, that is when no one comes out feeling like they participated in a flame war, and at least came out with more familiarity with the other's reasoning/source material. Respond in kind, treat others how you would like to be treated, all that jazz.

That being said, not all arguments are of equal quality. It has gotten to the point where topics like the health effects of smoking tobacco, or climate change, or the theory of evolution have a body of evidence, and decade(s) of dealing with the opposition. If someone goes "I should be allowed to smoke tobacco in a pub/café, I do it to prevent Parkinson's" will be met with downvotes, because of literal cancer. Now take something more recent, or controversial, and someone goes "I should be allowed to vape using an e-cigarette in a pub/café", that becomes marred in what sources someone is using to justify their claims, opposing opinions with different government bodies/research institutions. And that is something that has a lot of interested parties involved, where everyone involved is looking to promote the dissemination of peer-reviewed science. That is not getting into debates about more charged topics, like gender, religion, immigration, culture or race politics. All topics that people have very strong opinions on, which promote a certain echo chamber/hivemind to develop in biased communities, that are only met with the same level evangelicalism of operating systems /s.

As someone who prefers to lurk, even if I wanted to downvote I couldn't, at least here. That's fine, since it's not something I generally do anyway, but it's a bit odd. As for whether it should be used as a "disagree" button, clearly not, but try to get people to follow that and you'll be fighting an uphill battle. People want to hurt opinions that are different from their own, and so they will downvote accordingly, no matter whether it contributed to the overall discussion or not. In the end, post scores are about how popular of an opinion something was, which is useful to a degree, but it sucks when an unpopular opinion must be expanded because downvotes had hidden it from view.

On the one hand it's supposed to be for things that don't contribute to the discussion. In the other hand, it does say "X dislikes" over in the sidebar. I marry the two by trying to only dislike what doesn't contribute to the discussion. The result is a more enjoyable experience for me because I'm learning to not take disagreement personally and accept it as a positive thing because it adds to my perspective.
